correctness.rationale: A projection onto ker(sum) is I-v(sum) with sum(v)=1; permutation averaging over isometries fixes the unique symmetric centering P_n and does not increase operator norm. For sorted absolute inputs, write x as the convex combination of normalized signed indicators u_k/W_k using level differences a_k-a_(k+1); this reduces the operator norm exactly, not approximately, to signed-support tests. With k support and s negative after global sign, d=(k-2s)/n, output magnitudes 1+d (s times), 1-d (k-s times), d (n-k times); sorting at d=1/2 yields the claimed two rational F_{n,k,s} formulas. Direct exact fraction arithmetic, independent of the source checker, exhausted all ternary support vectors up to n=7 for 20 independently sampled descending rational/integer weight vectors each and matched every finite formula. n=2 contractive by (I-swap)/2; n=3 explicit maximum has two decisive tests, so norm one iff W3=2w1 or w2+w3=w1. For n>=4, the e1 and full sign vector force Wn=2w1 if contractive; at n=4 the (++-0) centered norm exceeds source norm by w4/2>0, while for n>=5 the (n-2 plus,2 minus) test exceeds by 2(n-4)w2/n>0. No extrapolation from finite experiments is needed.
